text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finns cheered but without euphoria when President Bill Clinton's Dodge van and President Boris Yeltsin's Zil limousine drove along Helsinki streets on Thursday.
- Helsinki summit visitors did not find the night life very exciting.
- Russian prime minister has given backing to plan to build oil pipeline from northern Russia province of Timan-Petshoran to the Gulf of Finland. @
- Hymn singing strengthened Finnish identity against the onslaught of foreign cultural influence during Russian rule in the 19th century, new study says.
- Man concerned by influence of drugs and sex on young people set fire to strip-tease restaurant in centre of Helsinki.
- Three Finnish men intend to ski across Greenland glacier.
- Politicians are not trying to push through Finnish EMU membership soley by legal arguments, but rather by seeking broad popular support through extensive EMU debate (editorial). @
- American paper industry lobby AF&PA still strongly blames Finland for being responsible for EU not lifting duties on paper imports.
- Finns have suddenly acquired a strong urge to do something about nature. Special travels to experience the nature becoming a phenomenon, opening up new markets for investors.
- Disappearance of children of moslem families living as reefugees in Finland found to have been sent home by their parents in order to avoid too much influence of western culture. @
- Finland's opposition to shipyard subsidies and its call to abolish them was discussed when President Martti Ahtisaari met U.S. Presiden Bill Clinton on Thursday.
- City of Helsinki to receive state support of 50 million markka to prepare for status as European culture city in 2000.
